targets.name: lares
targets.doc: ~/.config/theme/state.json: Theme.qml watches it, so the shell's crossfade starts when it lands (the first target)

targets.name: vscode
targets.doc: VS Code's workbench.colorTheme (the theme's assets.<mode>.vscodeTheme: a name VS Code has installed), set by an edit of the settings.json TEXT -- the file has comments and a trailing comma, so nothing is parsed and re-written; VS Code applies the change as the file lands -- about 0.4 s later, longer while its window is hidden: the SECOND target, so that it has taken the theme before the curtain shows its hidden window (ThemeControl, the hidden windows). theme-switch.py did this for two years; no file (VS Code not installed) is no failure; nothing is kept for `restore` (it is the user's long-lived file)

targets.name: wallpaper
targets.doc: the wallpaper shell.jsonc sets for this theme and mode (theme.wallpapers.<theme>.<light|dark>: a path or a list of paths; theme.wallpaperFit): of a list, one is drawn from the slot's shuffle bag (~/.local/state/theme/wallpaper-bag.json) when the theme, the mode or the Hyprland session changed, else the current pick stays. hyprpaper.conf is written for the daemon's next start and `hyprctl hyprpaper wallpaper` tells the running one (hyprpaper 0.8+; no transition of its own: the shell's crossfade is the transition). Nothing set for the theme and mode is 'skipped'; hyprpaper not running is no failure

targets.name: yazi
targets.doc: yazi's view of the current theme and mode's wallpapers (tools/theme/yazi/CHEATSHEET.md): the list file the wallpapers.yazi plugin marks files from, and the exact-path open rules between the BEGIN/END marks in yazi.toml's [open] prepend_rules that give those files "Remove from wallpapers" (themectl install sets the marks up; without them the rules are 'not set up', no failure)

targets.name: hyprland

include.line: pcall(require, "config/theme")   -- after require("config/appearance"); guarded, so a missing file is not an error

targets.doc: window borders, group borders, the shadow colour and Hyprglass's default_theme: a generated .lua, applied live by hyprctl eval (never hyprctl reload); a config.reloaded handler in it says the Hyprglass mode again after plugins.lua

targets.name: kitty
targets.doc: colours, cursor, selection and the 16 ANSI slots; kitty reloads its config on SIGUSR1

targets.name: btop
targets.doc: a theme named current in btop's themes directory, a link to the theme of the mode (assets.btopTheme): btop's stock theme where it ships one that matches (an absolute /usr/share/btop/themes path), else a custom one the repo ships in tools/theme/btop/ (a bare file name, made by tools/theme/pairgen.py), copied next to the link when first used; btop reloads on SIGUSR2

targets.name: starship
targets.doc: the whole prompt config (starship has no include); the symlink into HyprV/starship is replaced by a file themectl owns

targets.name: libadwaita
targets.doc: libadwaita's colours: GTK 4's user stylesheet (~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css, loaded over every GTK 4 app) sets libadwaita 1.10's CSS variables (--window-bg-color, --view-bg-color, --accent-bg-color, ...) from the pair's tokens: the surface, the carved list fill, the sunk panel, the exact accent. libadwaita apps (loupe, zenity) ignore the GTK theme, so this is what makes them follow a pair; colours only, no widget restyled; a plain GTK 4 app keeps its GTK theme. Written before the gtk target. What was there first is kept for `restore`

targets.name: gtk
targets.doc: gsettings: gtk-theme, color-scheme, icon-theme (the theme's assets: GTK takes installed names, not colours). gsettings is the ONE source the desktop follows: the shell reads icon-theme from it when it starts (tools/shell/lares-supervise exports QS_ICON_THEME), GTK apps follow it live

targets.name: nwg-look
targets.doc: nwg-look in step with the gtk target: its stored settings (what `nwg-look -a` applies) carry the pair's gtk-theme, icon-theme and color-scheme, and its export-gtk4-symlinks is off, so its Apply never replaces ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css by a link into a GTK theme (the original config is kept for `restore`). Its window shows what gsettings said when it opened: close and reopen it after a switch (doctor says when one is running). No nwg-look files is 'skipped'

targets.name: gnome-accent
targets.doc: libadwaita's accent: gsettings org.gnome.desktop.interface accent-color, the named GNOME accent (blue teal green yellow orange red pink purple slate) nearest by CIEDE2000 to the theme's accent token. for whatever reads that key; libadwaita reads it only when no settings portal answers (this desktop's xdg-desktop-portal-gtk does, without it), and the libadwaita target's stylesheet sets the pair's exact accent over it

targets.name: evince
targets.doc: Evince (Document Viewer) shows documents with inverted colours in the modes invertIn names: the default for a new document (gsettings org.gnome.Evince.Default inverted-colors), the copy evince keeps per document in its GVfs metadata (metadata::evince::inverted-colors) for every document GTK's recent list names, and every evince window open now (its inverted-colors window action over D-Bus). Skipped when evince is not installed

targets.name: gtk3-ini
targets.doc: the same two names in GTK 3's settings.ini, for a program started without a settings daemon (the file is edited in place: its other keys and comments stay)

targets.name: fastfetch
targets.doc: archlogo_current.png -> the theme's logo for this mode: the user's own (eva, everbox) or one the repo ships in tools/theme/fastfetch/ (the line logo in the mode's accent, made by tools/theme/pairgen.py --logos), copied next to the link when first used

targets.name: hyprlock
targets.doc: the fallback lock's colour variables ($FIELD, $BORDER, ...), until the shell's own lockscreen is deployed

targets.name: windows-vm
targets.doc: the word light or dark in the folder the Windows VM shares (the compose file's volume at /shared), for the small agent inside it (windows/ThemeSync.cs, windows/INSTALL.md) to apply. It works with the VM off, and no VM here is 'skipped'
